must_do: read the spec first and stop if it is missing — OpenSpec blocks the domain artifact until `specs` completes

read the living model openspec/domain/model.md at C0 and classify every needed concept NEW / EXTENDS / REUSES / CONFLICT before modeling (on a project's first change, C0 declares everything NEW and creates the living model)
read the schema's own guidance for the artifact (openspec instructions domain --change <id>) rather than restating the required sections from memory
treat the artifact's existence, path and ordering as the schema's concern (domain requires specs; tasks requires domain) and not re-derive it
identify the Moment-Intervals first (read the spec's scenarios as events), and get that list approved (C1) before deriving anything else
stop for approval at all five checkpoints (C0 reconciliation, C1 MIs, C2 concepts, C3 attributes+links, C4 mapping) — none is skipped for being a small model
at C3 show the attributes table with an explicit stored/derived column, and the links table with multiplicity and togetherness

run the four self-review scans before presenting a checkpoint (MI without participants, two concepts sharing attributes, an unmarked derived numeric/positional attribute, a two-valued Description), and present unresolved findings rather than hiding them
before C4's approval, report spec coverage as a table (Requirement/Scenario -> concept or MI -> covered?) and surface every gap as a finding the user decides on
map each archetype onto the kit: MI -> Repository method + ViewModel action (never a UseCase class, Rule 9), PPT -> data/model/*Response.kt, Role -> field/nested object, Description -> enum
mark every derived attribute (a count that is an aggregation, a rank that is a position in a sort) explicitly as derived rather than stored

write two files at Phase 5 — openspec/changes/<id>/domain.md (the delta) and openspec/domain/model.md (the living vocabulary) — and only what C4 approved, then re-run kmp_route.py so .kmp/route.json sees it
record `Domain model: none` with one sentence when the capability genuinely has no domain concepts
must_not: start from the spec's nouns / entity list instead of Moment-Intervals
fold C3 (attributes + links) into the C4 mapping checkpoint, or skip C3 because the derived/stored calls look mechanical
silently resolve a CONFLICT (same name different meaning, or two names for one concept) instead of stopping to ask the user
restate a REUSED concept inside the change's model so it reads standalone — it stays defined once, in openspec/domain/model.md
treat the living model as a requirement source: it emits no SHALL/MUST, and a spec that needs a concept the model lacks still decides
silently re-open an already-approved checkpoint — editing the MI list after C1 passed without saying so and re-running C1
write any new concept or field in Phase 5 that C4 did not approve
model a Moment-Interval as a UseCase class (Rule 9 forbids the UseCase layer)
add a parallel Response DTO for something that is a Role on an existing party
invent a requirement to fill a table — a gap goes under Open questions with the default taken
edit feature/**, the spec, or the design; this skill writes only domain.md
omit domain.md silently when the model is trivial — silence is indistinguishable from skipping it

pass_criteria: domain.md exists in the change directory with Moment-Intervals first, every derived attribute marked, a filled archetype->KMP mapping table, and no UseCase layer; all four checkpoints were presented with Evidence/Summary/Ask and approved; the self-review scans ran; spec coverage was reported with gaps named; re-running kmp_route.py reports artifacts.domain present.

should: what should the data model be
